"I don't think that there's a world where you do safety and people are accepting of AI companies just doing it on honor code," she said at the Politico Decoded Summit on Wednesday. "We can't be checking our own homework."

Heck observed that AI capabilities are increasing at a pace that is accelerating and it's "existential" to regulate the technology. "We have to balance the risk now," she said. "We want to work with government to figure out what makes sense."

Even so, Heck believes the U.S. needs to maintain its dominance in the global AI race. "The U.S. needs to stay in the lead on AI, and you can't do safety from second place," she said, echoing comments made by President Donald Trump and his administration.
